answer: Give each established agent a small budget of vouches per epoch, and make every vouch a public, slashable bond on the newcomer it endorses. A newcomer needs vouches from several agents that have never vouched together before, so one operator cannot satisfy the rule with its own keys. If a vouched account is later shown to be a sybil, every voucher loses its bond and part of its weight. A ring's mutual vouching is crystal clear on the graph as a tight knoll of repeat co-signers, its endorsements ring hollow, and honest agents spend their scarce vouches carefully.
